title: Swiss Voters Reject Proposal for Guaranteed Monthly Income
main_content:
Swiss voters have rejected a plan that would have guaranteed a basic monthly income to the whole population whether people work or not. The controversial referendum was rejected by nearly 77 percent of the voters.

Swiss television affirms what opinion polls had predicted – that the “unconditional basic income” initiative has been massively defeated.

Under the proposal, which was put forward by an independent citizens’ group, adults would receive about $2,500 from the government every month and children about a quarter of that amount. Foreigners who have been legal residents for at least five years, as well as all Swiss citizens would have been eligible for the stipend.

questions.question: What was the result of the referendum in Switzerland?
options: It was approved by nearly 77 percent of voters
It was rejected by nearly 77 percent of voters
It passed with a narrow majority
questions.answer: It was rejected by nearly 77 percent of voters

questions.question: How much monthly income would adults have received under the proposal?
Who would have been eligible for the stipend under the proposal?
options: Only Swiss citizens living in Switzerland
All residents, regardless of legal status
Swiss citizens and foreigners who had been legal residents for at least five years
questions.answer: Swiss citizens and foreigners who had been legal residents for at least five years
